$comment: Hours: decimal hours in IST (21.5 = 9:30 pm). A range past 24 runs after midnight. 'days' overrides 'h' for a weekday (0 = Sunday); [] means closed. Sources: Google Maps listings checked 14-15 Oct 2026, shop signboards and press. Verify with each host before launch. Places with a 'city' are outside the Madurai region: their hours and coordinates were compiled from public listings and guides in November 2026, are approximate, and each carries a tip saying so.

moments.t: The quiet hours. Only the hotels, the flower market and Paravai's night vegetable market are awake. Halwa returns at 4.
4 am. Prema Vilas lights its stoves and Koodal Azhagar opens its doors.
5 am. Meenakshi temple and Thiruparankundram open for the morning ritual.
Dawn. Sunrise on Samanar Hills while the jasmine trade peaks at Mattuthavani.
Breakfast. Idli on West Masi Street, or mutton at Sulthan.
Late morning. Masi street shops roll up their shutters, jigarthanda counters open and the Gandhi Museum welcomes visitors.
Lunch. Banana-leaf meals in the lanes around the temple.
Afternoon. Temples reopen at 4; bun parotta's first batch is on the griddle.
Evening. Butter buns come off the griddles; Teppakulam fills with families.
6:45 pm. The Nayak palace sound and light show begins.
9 pm. Palliarai: Shiva is carried by palanquin to Meenakshi's chamber.
Late night. Parotta and kari dosai keep the city awake.
After midnight. Sulthan still serves parotta until 1 am.

places.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
places.story: The heart of Madurai: 14 gopurams and a city built in concentric squares around it. Around 9–9:30 pm, the Palliarai ceremony carries Shiva by palanquin to Meenakshi's chamber.
tips: Phones and footwear go in lockers at the gates
Stay for the 9 pm Palliarai

image.alt: The east gopuram of the Meenakshi Amman Temple

places.name: Koodal Azhagar Temple
places.address: Koodal Alagar Perumal Koil St, Periyar, Madurai 625001
places.story: A Divya Desam of Vishnu a short walk from Meenakshi. Climb the tower to see him seated, standing and reclining on three levels.
tips: Small ticket to climb the tower

image.alt: The tower of Koodal Azhagar Temple

places.name: Immaiyil Nanmai Tharuvar Temple
places.story: One of the city's oldest shrines, where Shiva himself is shown worshipping the lingam. The earth temple among Madurai's five-element shrines.

image.alt: The entrance of Immaiyil Nanmai Tharuvar Temple

places.name: Thiruvappudaiyar Temple, Sellur
places.address: Thiru Aapudayaar Kovil Agraharam Rd, Sellur, Madurai 625002
places.story: A Shiva temple praised in the Devaram hymns, on the north bank of the Vaigai.

image.alt: The entrance arch of Thiruvappudaiyar Temple, Sellur

places.name: Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam
places.hours: Tank open round the clock; evenings busiest
places.story: A vast 17th-century temple tank from Thirumalai Nayak's reign, with an island mandapam. Evenings bring snack carts; the float festival comes in Thai (January–February).
tips: Come at sunset
Float festival in Thai

image.alt: The Teppakulam tank and its island mandapam lit up at night

places.name: Pandi Muneeswarar Temple
places.story: Madurai's guardian folk deity, beloved by locals who come for justice and protection.

image.alt: Devotees at the Pandi Muneeswarar shrine

places.name: Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple
places.story: First of Murugan's six abodes, cut into a rock hill, where Murugan married Deivanai.

image.alt: The colourful gopuram of Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple against the hill

places.name: Yoga Narasimha Temple, Yanaimalai
places.story: A rock-cut cave temple carved into Elephant Hill in 770 CE. Go before sunset for the view.

image.file: Narasingam Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple Madurai (2).jpg
image.alt: Yoga Narasimha temple at the foot of Yanaimalai

places.name: Kalamegha Perumal Temple, Thirumohur
places.story: A Divya Desam of Vishnu with a large temple tank, mentioned in ancient Tamil classics.

image.alt: The entrance tower of Kalamegha Perumal Temple, Thirumohur

places.name: Kallazhagar Temple, Alagar Kovil
places.address: Alagar Kovil Main Rd, Alagar Kovil 625301
places.story: Vishnu's forest temple. At Chithirai, Kallazhagar rides a golden horse into the Vaigai to a city-wide welcome.

image.alt: The Rajagopuram of the Kallazhagar Temple at Alagar Kovil

places.name: Pazhamudircholai Murugan Temple
places.story: The sixth abode of Murugan, up the forest road above Alagar Kovil, where a boy-Murugan tested the poet Avvaiyar.

image.alt: The gopuram of Pazhamudircholai Murugan Temple

places.name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
places.hours: 9 am–5 pm; light show 6:45 pm (English), 8 pm (Tamil)
places.story: Built in 1636 by Tirumala Nayak, blending Dravidian and Islamic styles. Its courtyard comes alive for the evening sound and light show.

image.alt: The giant pillars and arches of Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal

places.name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
places.story: Gandhi adopted the loincloth in Madurai in 1921. Nearby: the Tamil Annai statue and World Tamil Sangam. Recent visitors report the main building under renovation.

image.file: Gandhi Memorial Museum Madurai TamilNadu India.jpg
image.alt: The Gandhi Memorial Museum in the 1670 Tamukkam palace

places.name: Samanar Hills (Jain beds)
places.story: A rock hill with Jain stone beds and inscriptions more than 2,000 years old, and the best sunrise near Madurai.
tips: Carry water
Go at sunrise

image.alt: Sunset over the plains from the top of Samanar Hills

places.name: Keeladi Museum (Keezhadi)
places.story: Finds from a Sangam-age town on the Vaigai, more than 2,000 years old: brick walls, ring wells, and pottery scratched with Tamil-Brahmi letters. The open-air excavation site is about a kilometre away.
tips: Watch the intro film first
Combine with the dig site

image.alt: The Keeladi museum buildings in Chettinad style

places.name: Pathu Thoon (Ten Pillars)
places.area: Mahal area, behind the Nayakkar Mahal
places.address: Pathu Thoon Street, Mahal Area, Madurai 625001
places.hours: Open street, any time; best in daylight
places.story: Ten granite pillars about 12 m tall, all that stands of the Rangavilasam wing of Thirumalai Nayak's palace, where his brother Muthialu Nayak lived. Today they rise from a lane of textile shops.
tips: Pair with the Nayakkar Mahal
Look up between the shops

image.alt: The granite Ten Pillars rising above the shops of Pathu Thoon Street

places.name: Avaniyapuram Jallikattu
places.hours: Village lanes, daylight. Jallikattu: mid-January, during Pongal
places.story: Madurai's first jallikattu of every Pongal, run through the village's own barricaded street with spectators packed on the terraces.

image.alt: A tamer clings to a bull at Avaniyapuram jallikattu

places.name: Alanganallur Jallikattu Vadivasal
places.hours: Village gate, daylight. Jallikattu: mid-January, during Pongal
places.story: The most famous vadivasal in Tamil Nadu. Once a year at Pongal, bulls burst from this gate and tamers try to hold on to the hump. The other days, it is a quiet village lane with the gate and galleries.
tips: January: arrive before dawn
Watch from the galleries only

image.alt: A tamer holds on to a bull at Alanganallur jallikattu

places.name: Palamedu Jallikattu Vadivasal
places.hours: Village lanes, daylight. Jallikattu: mid-January, during Pongal
places.story: Palamedu's vadivasal opens on Mattu Pongal, the day of the bulls, with galleries that hold one of the biggest crowds of the season.

image.alt: Bulls and handlers in the Palamedu jallikattu arena

places.name: Kalaignar Centenary Jallikattu Arena
places.story: A 67-acre arena the state opened in 2024 for jallikattu, with galleries under the hills. Outside the season visitors can walk the ground and see where the bulls run.
tips: Combine with Alanganallur vadivasal

image.alt: Jallikattu in Madurai (representative photo)

places.name: Mattuthavani flower market
places.hours: Round the clock most days (Sun, Mon 3 am–10 pm); busiest at dawn
places.story: Madurai malli, the city's GI-tagged jasmine, changes hands in heaps before sunrise.

image.alt: Heaps of Madurai jasmine at the Mattuthavani flower market

places.name: Prema Vilas
places.story: Hot wheat halwa served on a leaf, from 4 am.

image.alt: The Prema Vilas shopfront on Town Hall Road

places.name: Aathi Kalathu Nei Mittai Kadai (red board)
places.story: The original red-board shop near the temple's Nandi: nei mittai and halwa, plus spicy kizhangu pottalam until 1 pm.

image.alt: The red signboard of Aathi Kalathu Original Nei Mittai Kadai

places.name: Murugan Idli Shop (original)
places.story: Soft idli on a banana leaf with a row of chutneys and podi.

image.alt: The original Murugan Idli Shop on West Masi Street

places.name: Sulthan Hotel
places.story: A mutton breakfast from 8 am, and parotta until 1 am.

image.alt: The lit signboard of Yanaikal Sulthan Hotel at night

places.name: Jaya Vilas
places.story: A meals club down a narrow lane near the temple, serving since 1950. Try the ayirai fish curry.

image.alt: The Jeya Vilas Sappadu Club signboard on East Avani Moola Street

places.name: Hotel Sri Janakiram
places.story: Banana-leaf non-veg meals with three gravies; try the mutton chukka.

image.alt: The neon sign of Hotel Sri Janakiram

places.name: Konar Kadai
places.story: Where kari dosai is said to have started.

image.alt: Konar Kadai lit up at night

places.name: New Janani Mess
places.story: Mutton chukka and vengaya kari in the busy onion market, until midnight.

image.alt: New Janani Mess busy at night

places.name: P. Power Hotel
places.story: A long mutton menu, from brain roast to kari dosai.

image.alt: P. Power Hotel and mutton stall at night

places.name: Muthukumar Bun Parotta
places.story: A ten-seat stall; flaky bun parotta with two salnas.

places.name: Famous Jigarthanda, Vilakkuthoon
places.story: The city's signature cold drink of milk, almond gum, nannari syrup and ice cream.

image.alt: Crowds outside Famous Jigarthanda

places.name: Sri Thirumalai Madai Karuppasamy Paruthi Paal
places.hours: 9 am–10:30 pm; Sat from 4 pm; closed Sundays
places.story: Warm cottonseed milk with palm jaggery and dry ginger.

image.alt: The Karuppasamy paruthi paal stall

places.name: Kalapilla Tea Shop
places.hours: 5:30 am–10 pm (Sun to 2 pm); butter bun from evening
places.story: A tea shop of more than 50 years; butter bun with hot cow's milk is the evening ritual.

places.name: Lakshmi Butter Bun, Sellur
places.story: Buns toasted in butter with sugar or palm jaggery, eaten standing.

places.name: Heritage Madurai
places.story: Tamil-style rooms and villas among old trees, with a pool built like a temple tank.

image.alt: The Heritage Madurai sign at the entrance

places.name: Gateway Madurai, Pasumalai (Taj)
places.story: Colonial-style rooms on a hilltop, with peacocks wandering the lawns.

image.alt: The colonial-style main building of Gateway Madurai on Pasumalai hill

places.name: Gopuram Grand
places.story: Steps from the temple; its restaurant looks straight at the west gopuram.

image.alt: The Gopuram Grand hotel facade lit at night

places.name: East Masi Street groceries & spices
places.address: E Masi St, Madurai Main, Madurai 625001
places.hours: Most shops 9:30 am–10 pm; many close on Sundays
places.story: Madurai's wholesale lane for groceries, spices, dry fruits and flours. Families stock up here for weddings and festivals, and the shops deliver across the city.
tips: Buy spices by weight
Many shops shut on Sunday

places.name: South Masi Street sarees & textiles
places.address: S Masi St, Mahal Area, Madurai 625001
places.hours: Big showrooms 9:30 am–9:30 pm, open daily
places.story: Multi-floor saree showrooms and decades-old wholesale cloth shops line the southern Masi street: silk, cotton, wedding and everyday wear.
tips: Busiest before festivals
Ask for Madurai cotton

image.alt: Garment shops on a Madurai market street

places.name: Sungudi saree makers, Munichalai
places.story: Madurai's GI-tagged sungudi tie-dye sarees, made by the city's Sourashtra weaving families. Buy straight from makers' shops.

places.name: South Avani Moola Street jewellery
places.address: S Avani Moola St, near Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai 625001
places.story: The gold street just south of the temple: rows of jewellers selling temple-style necklaces, wedding sets and everyday gold.

places.name: Valayalkara Street bangles
places.address: Big Valayalkara St, Madurai Main, Madurai 625001
places.story: Bangle street beside West Avani Moola: glass, metal, thread and bridal bangles in every size, wholesale and retail.

places.name: Kamarajar Salai steel & brass
places.story: Stores stacked with steel, brass and cast-iron cookware and lamps. Families come here for wedding 'seer varisai' sets.

places.name: Pudhu Mandapam & Kunnathur Chathiram
places.address: E Chitrai St and Kunnathur Chathiram, Madurai 625001
places.hours: Shops about 9 am–9 pm; moving during restoration
places.story: A 17th-century pillared hall facing the temple's east tower, long home to tailors, brassware, bangles and books. Its shops are moving to nearby Kunnathur Chathiram while the hall is restored.

image.alt: The pillared Pudhu Mandapam hall opposite the temple

places.name: Central Vegetable Market
places.address: Melur Main Rd, KK Nagar, Madurai 625020
places.hours: From before dawn into the evening; best early morning
places.story: The old temple-area market, moved out to Melur Road: wholesale and retail vegetables, with the fruit and flower markets on the same road.

image.file: A man weighing tomatoes using his Tharasu in Madurai.jpg
image.alt: A vendor weighing tomatoes in Madurai (representative photo)

places.name: Paravai wholesale vegetable market
places.hours: Night market: from 8 pm through the next afternoon; busiest after 10 pm
places.story: One of south Tamil Nadu's biggest vegetable markets. It comes alive overnight as lorries unload, with small eateries serving the night traders.

places.name: Arittapatti Biodiversity Heritage Site
places.story: Tamil Nadu's first biodiversity heritage site: bare granite hills full of birds, a lake, and Jain caves with Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions.

places.name: Kutladampatti Falls
places.story: A waterfall in the Sirumalai foothills, nicknamed Madurai's Kutralam, at its best after the monsoon.

image.file: Kutladampatti near Vadipatti by Essaar on 17102011 2.jpg
image.alt: Water cascading over rocks at Kutladampatti

places.name: Thiruvathavur Thirumarainathar Temple
places.story: The birthplace of the saint-poet Manikkavasagar, with a pure Pandya-style Shiva temple and many sacred tanks.

places.name: Dindigul Rock Fort
places.story: A 17th-century fort of the Madurai Nayaks on a single giant rock, later held by Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan and the British.

image.alt: The temple and walls on top of Dindigul Rock Fort

places.name: Sirumalai Hills
places.story: A quiet hill station of 18 hairpin bends, forests, mist and a viewpoint over Dindigul, the nearest hills to Madurai.

image.file: Sirumalai Hills,viewed from Mathamalai Annai Veilankanni Church,Dindigul,TN,India.jpg
image.alt: The Sirumalai hills seen from Dindigul

places.name: Srivilliputhur Andal Temple
places.story: Birthplace of Andal, the only woman among the Alvar saints. Its rajagopuram is the emblem of Tamil Nadu.

image.alt: The rajagopuram of Srivilliputhur Andal temple

places.name: Pillayarpatti Karpaga Vinayagar Temple
places.story: One of the oldest rock-cut Ganesha shrines in India, cut into a hillock in Chettinad and loved by the Nagarathar community.

image.alt: The gopuram of Pillayarpatti Karpaga Vinayagar temple

places.name: Kundrakudi Shanmuganathar Temple
places.story: A hillock temple of six-faced Murugan on his peacock, about 150 rock-cut steps up, a few minutes from Pillayarpatti.

image.alt: The temple car at Kundrakudi Murugan temple

places.name: Chettinad Palace, Kanadukathan
places.hours: 10 am–6 pm (view from outside; some mansions open for a fee)
places.story: The grand mansions of the Nagarathar merchants: Burma teak, Italian marble, Belgian glass and Athangudi tiles, in streets of palaces.

image.file: India Tamil Nadu Kanadukathan Raja Palace.JPG
image.alt: The Raja palace mansion at Kanadukathan, Chettinad

places.name: Athangudi Tile Workshops
places.story: Watch Chettinad's famous handmade cement tiles being poured, patterned and sun-dried by hand, the way they have been for generations.

image.alt: Hand-made Athangudi tiles in Chettinad patterns

places.name: Thirumayam Fort
places.story: A 17th-century hill fort of great boulders, with cannons, a rock-cut Shiva shrine and views over Chettinad.

image.alt: The boulder walls of Thirumayam Fort

places.name: Vaigai Dam
places.story: The dam that holds back the Vaigai, Madurai's river, with gardens, a children's park and breezy walks below the hills.

image.alt: Vaigai Dam and its gardens

places.name: Kumbakkarai Falls
places.story: A forest waterfall at the foot of the Kodaikanal hills with natural rock pools for a cool bath.

places.name: Sathuragiri Sundara Mahalingam Temple
places.hours: Pilgrim trek on set days only (around new and full moon)
places.story: A forest pilgrimage to Shiva, the abode of the 18 Siddhars, reached by a steep 8 km trek in the Western Ghats.

image.alt: The forest path at Sathuragiri

places.name: Vettangudi Bird Sanctuary
places.story: Village tanks where painted storks, herons and migrant birds nest in winter, watched from towers on the bund.

places.name: Thiruchuli Thirumeninathar Temple
places.story: An ancient Shiva temple sung in the Devaram, and the birthplace of Ramana Maharshi, whose childhood home is preserved nearby.

image.alt: Thiruchuli Thirumeninathar temple, north side

places.name: Kalayarkoil Sornakaleeswarar Temple
places.story: A temple of three Shiva shrines with a towering gopuram, linked to the Marudhu brothers who fought the British.

places.name: Sivaganga Palace (Gowri Vilasam)
places.story: The palace of the Sivaganga kingdom, tied to Queen Velu Nachiyar and the Marudhu brothers, India's early fighters against the British.

places.name: Suruli Falls
places.story: A two-tier waterfall from the Meghamalai hills near Cumbum, reached by a forest walk, with siddhar caves and shrines around it.

places.name: Ayyanar Falls, Rajapalayam
places.hours: Forest gate open on limited days; check before going
places.story: A forest waterfall beside the old Neer Kaatha Ayyanar temple in the Western Ghats above Rajapalayam.

places.name: Thalaiyar (Rat Tail) Falls
places.area: On the Kodaikanal ghat road, 66 km northwest
places.address: Viewpoint on the Laws Ghat Road, Dindigul district 624101
places.hours: Daylight; seen from the ghat road
places.story: One of the tallest waterfalls in Tamil Nadu, a thin silver ribbon down a sheer cliff, seen from a viewpoint on the road to Kodaikanal.

image.alt: Thalaiyar (Rat Tail) Falls down a sheer cliff

places.name: Kodaikanal
places.hours: Lake area open from morning to evening
places.story: The 'princess of hill stations': a star-shaped lake, pine forests, misty viewpoints and cool air, above Madurai's plains.

image.alt: Kodaikanal lake among pine forest

places.name: Palani Dhandayuthapani Temple
places.story: Murugan's third abode, on a hill above Palani, reached by steps, a winch train or a rope car; one of the most visited temples in India.

image.alt: Palani hill with the Murugan temple on top

places.name: Meghamalai (High Wavy Mountains)
places.hours: Daylight; forest check post on the ghat road
places.story: Misty tea estates, lakes and forest on the 'high wavy mountains' of the Western Ghats, where elephants still cross the road.

image.alt: The Meghamalai mountains of the Western Ghats

places.name: Kazhugumalai Vettuvan Koil
places.story: An 8th-century Pandya temple carved from the top of a single granite hill, left unfinished, with Jain carvings on the same rock.

image.alt: The monolithic Vettuvan Koil carved into the hilltop at Kazhugumalai

places.name: Sittanavasal Cave Paintings
places.story: A Jain rock-cut cave with paintings over a thousand years old, including a famous lotus-pond ceiling: the 'Ajanta of the south'.

image.file: A aesthetic rock view of Sittanavasal 1.JPG
image.alt: The rock hill at Sittanavasal

places.name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam
places.hours: About 6 am–9 pm, with breaks for worship
places.story: A temple town on an island between the Kaveri and the Kollidam: seven walled enclosures, 21 gopurams and a 72-metre tower, one of the largest working temples in the world.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Rockfort and Ucchi Pillayar Temple
places.story: An 83-metre rock rising straight out of the old town. More than 400 steps cut into the stone climb past Pallava cave temples to the Ganesha shrine and a view over the Kaveri.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Jambukeswarar Temple, Thiruvanaikaval
places.story: One of the five temples of the elements: here Shiva is water, and a spring keeps the sanctum wet all year.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Kallanai (Grand Anicut)
places.story: A stone dam across the Kaveri built by the Chola king Karikalan about 2,000 years ago, and still watering the delta today.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Church
places.story: A late 19th-century Gothic church with a tall spire and stained glass, modelled on the basilica at Lourdes, facing the Rockfort tank.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Parthasarathy Vilas
places.story: An old tiffin house by the Thiruvanaikaval temple, known across Trichy for its ghee-roast butter dosa.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Michael's Ice Cream
places.story: A Trichy landmark by Main Guard Gate where generations have queued for plain, cheap, old-style ice cream.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: NSB Road and Teppakulam bazaar
places.story: The shopping streets under the Rockfort: sarees and textiles, brass, jewellery and the Chinna Kadai lanes.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Sangam Hotel, Trichy
places.story: A long-established full-service hotel with a pool, central for the railway junction, the Rockfort and Srirangam.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple (Big Temple)
places.story: Raja Raja Chola's granite temple, finished in 1010: a 66-metre tower, a giant Nandi carved from one stone, and a place on UNESCO's list of Great Living Chola Temples.
tips: Come at sunrise or late afternoon, when the granite turns gold.
Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Thanjavur Palace and Saraswathi Mahal Library
places.story: The palace of the Nayak and Maratha kings: a gallery of Chola bronzes, a bell tower, and one of Asia's oldest libraries with thousands of palm-leaf manuscripts.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Schwartz Church
places.area: Sivaganga Park, by the Big Temple
places.story: Built in 1779 by Raja Serfoji for his teacher, the missionary Christian Friedrich Schwartz, with a marble relief of the king at the old man's bedside.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Saint Thyagaraja's Samadhi, Thiruvaiyaru
places.story: The resting place of the composer Thyagaraja on the bank of the Kaveri. Each January, hundreds of musicians gather here to sing his Pancharatna kritis together.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Bombay Sweets
places.story: Started in 1949 by Guru Dayal Sharma of Mathura, and famous for chandrakala: a crisp, syrup-soaked half-moon filled with khoa.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Poompuhar handicrafts showroom
places.story: The state's own crafts showroom: Thanjavur paintings in gold leaf, art plates, bronzes and the nodding Thanjavur dolls.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Veena makers of South Main Street
places.story: Family workshops that carve the Thanjavur veena from a single block of jackwood, a craft with its own GI tag.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Svatma, Thanjavur
places.address: 4/1116 Blake Higher Secondary School Road, Maharnonbu Chavadi, Thanjavur 613001
places.story: A heritage hotel in a restored old mansion, with vegetarian Thanjavur food and evenings of music and dance.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple
places.story: The Shiva temple that gives Kumbakonam its name: the lingam is said to be shaped from the pot of nectar that came to rest here.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Sarangapani Temple
places.story: One of the 108 Divya Desams, with a towering gateway and a sanctum built as a stone chariot drawn by horses and elephants.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Mahamaham Tank
places.story: A six-acre temple tank ringed by sixteen small pavilions. Once every twelve years, lakhs of pilgrims bathe here for the Mahamaham festival; the next is due in 2028.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram
places.story: A 12th-century Chola temple on UNESCO's list: a hall built as a chariot with stone wheels, friezes of dancers, and steps that ring like musical notes.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Swamimalai Murugan Temple
places.story: One of Murugan's six abodes, on a small hill reached by sixty steps, one for each year of the Tamil cycle. Here the son taught his father the meaning of Om.
tips: Hours and the map pin come from public listings and guides, which differ. Please confirm before you go.

places.name: Sri Mangalambika Vilas Coffee Hotel
places.area: In the lane to Kumbeswarar temple
places.story: A small vegetarian coffee hotel with a board that says "Since 1914", serving tiffin on plantain leaves and Kumbakonam degree coffee in brass tumblers.
